papers.title: [Clinical evidence of acupuncture and moxibustion for depressive disorder: controversy, reflection and prospect].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Wang S, Wu Q, Ning B, Ma R, Wang C, Liang X et al.
papers.abstract: To clarify the clinical evidence required for integrating acupuncture and moxibustion treatment for depressive disorder into the mainstream psychiatric diagnostic and therapeutic system, as well as the existing deficiencies, this paper summarizes the current state of evidence for acupuncture and moxibustion treatment for depressive disorder from three perspectives: clinical guidelines, systematic reviews, and clinical trials. The differentiation of recommendations of different guidelines and its causes are analyzed, and the key issues such as the design and implementation of clinical research, efficacy evaluation, the integration of mechanisms with clinical practice, and the heterogeneity of acupuncture and moxibustion techniques and protocols are discussed. On this basis, the paper proposes that by conducting high-quality clinical research, constructing a multidimensional efficacy evaluation system, promoting the integration of mechanistic studies with clinical practice, and strengthening interdisciplinary collaboration and the translation of research outcomes, the therapeutic characteristics, target populations, and clinical value of acupuncture and moxibustion treatment for depressive disorder can be further clarified. This will provide a reference for improving the relevant clinical evidence system and promoting standardized application.

summary.results: 가이드라인 권고의 차이와 원인을 정리하고, 연구 설계·효과평가·기전과 임상 연계·침구 기법과 프로토콜의 이질성 등 핵심 쟁점을 제시했다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 침·뜸의 우울장애 적용은 근거 축적과 표준화가 더 필요하며, 임상에서는 기존 지침과 연구 수준의 한계를 함께 고려해야 한다.
summary.limitations: 실제 효과를 새로 추정한 것이 아니라 기존 지침·문헌·시험을 종합한 논의 중심의 요약이라는 점이 한계이다.

papers.title: [Development and application of a fumigation moxibustion device for small animals].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Wang W, Zhang X, Geng J, Sun Y, Wu S, Zhou M et al.
papers.abstract: A localized and quantitative fumigation moxibustion device for small animals was developed. The device consists of four components: an outer shell, a fumigation moxibustion chamber, fixing component, and adhesive component. It provides accurate positioning and stable moxibustion distance, enables real-time observation of the burning status and progress of moxa sticks, accommodates moxa sticks with different diameters, and has the advantages of convenient operation and high safety. However, the device is mainly applicable to acupoints on the head, face and back of laboratory animals, while its application to abdominal acupoints remains limited due to issues such as smoke backflow and difficulty in attachment.

papers.title: [Textual research on the origin and development of Xi-cleft point theory].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Liu S, Li R, Wu H, Qiu W, Wang T, Song Z et al.
papers.abstract: Xi-cleft point redefines the practical connotation of acupoint theory based on terminological system within the classical acupuncture framework. Xi-cleft point was proposed in Huangdi Mingtang Jing (The Yellow Emperor's Acupoints Canon of Mingtang), and was primarily intended to re-categorize the acupoints below the elbows and knees that were newly introduced beyond those recorded in Huangdi Neijing (The Yellow Emperor's Internal Classic) despite lacking clearly shared therapeutic indications in practice. But, the common therapeutic indications of this supplemented Xi-cleft points are unclear. The current theory of Xi-cleft point, "Xi-cleft points treat acute diseases", was summarized by Japanese acupuncture practitioners, and was introduced to China with the publication of corresponding Chinese translations of Japanese books of acupuncture and moxibustion. Later in 1984, YANG Jiasan edited Shuxue Xue (Science of Acupoints) and determined the indications of this special point, "Xi-cleft points of yin meridians treat blood disorders, while those of yang meridians treat pain". The common therapeutic indications of Xi-cleft points were analogically generalized by Chinese and Japanese medical scholars in the modern times based on the practical experience with some Xi-cleft points. In the time of Huangdi Mingtang Jing, Xi-cleft point was proposed to improve the theoretical framework of acupoint theory. Since there is lack of the anatomical distribution characteristics among Xi-cleft points regarding to the correspondence of the body to nature and similar indications, these Xi-cleft points do not necessarily share common therapeutic indications. Therefore, it needs to be validated in practice to identify whether the therapeutic characteristics of one specific Xi-cleft point are consistent with the current theory of Xi-cleft point, rather than regard it with the specific indication of the acupoint itself.

summary.results: 계혈은 고전에서 침구 이론 체계를 보완하기 위해 제시되었고, 현대의 '급성병 치료'와 음경혈은 혈증·양경혈은 통증이라는 설명은 후대의 추론과 경험적 일반화에 기반한 것으로 정리되었다.

papers.title: [Formulation of clinical questions and outcomes on Clinical Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Peptic Ulcer by Combination of Acupuncture and Medication].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Wan R, Sun L, Hou Y, Yan X, Ye J, Lai R et al.
papers.abstract:
To formulate the clinical questions and outcomes of Clinical Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Peptic Ulcer by Combination of Acupuncture and Medication based on Specification of Formulation and Evaluation for the Clinical Practice Guideline of Acupuncture and Moxibustion issued by the National Standardization Administration.
With a combination of survey-based research, expert consultation, and consensus-building methods, by targeting gastroenterologists, patients with peptic ulcer, and physicians in department of acupuncture and moxibustion as survey participants, and through investigating the current staus and existing questions in treatment of peptic ulcers, the clinical issues were collected. Subsequently, two rounds of questionnaires were conducted within the expert panel.
A total of 156 survey questionnaires were collected. The questionnaires highlighted that the conventional medications demonstrated limited efficacy in alleviating gastrointestinal symptoms in patients with peptic ulcer, and the concerns regarding potential adverse effects of these medications represented a major clinical issue; furthermore, the lack of standardized protocols for combination of acupuncture and medication for treating peptic ulcer constituted a primary clinical challenge. Hence, 25 clinical questions and 16 key outcomes were formulated. Following two rounds of expert consensus, clinical questions and outcomes that met the final inclusion criteria, specifically, those with an average importance score >7 and a coefficient of variation <0.30, were selected, covering 3 clinical questions and 8 key outcomes.
This study formulates the prioritized clinical questions and key outcomes for Clinical Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Peptic Ulcer by Combination of Acupuncture and Medication so as to lay a solid foundation for the subsequent development of scientific and practical recommendations in the guideline.

papers.title: [Distribution characteristics and protection strategies of provincial-level and above acupuncture-moxibustion intangible cultural heritage projects in China].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Zhao Z, Shao C, Hou Y, Wen S, Zhang Z
papers.abstract: This study systematically collected and analyzed 165 provincial-level and above acupuncture-moxibustion intangible cultural heritage projects from 31 provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the central government in China from 2006 to 2025, and conducted an in-depth study from four dimensions: spatial distribution, temporal evolution, level structure, and technical type. The results showed that acupuncture-moxibustion intangible cultural heritage projects presented obvious "overall dispersion, local aggregation" distribution characteristics in space, with Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, Shandong Province, Jiangsu Province, etc. being high-density areas, reflecting the profound influence of regional culture, medical schools, and ethnic medicine traditions. The total number of projects showed an upward trend, especially with explosive growth during 2021-2025, which was closely related to national policies on the inheritance and innovation of traditional Chinese medicine. The level structure was dominated by provincial-level projects, accounting for 91.5%; although national-level projects were fewer in number, they played a leading role. The technical types covered seven major categories, including acupuncture methods, moxibustion methods, cupping methods, bloodletting, ethnic characteristic therapies, etc. demonstrating a rich and diverse technical ecology and the "diversity in unity" pattern of Chinese medicine. This study revealed problems in the current protection of acupuncture-moxibustion intangible cultural heritage, and "emphasizing application submission while neglecting protection". It also notes the prominent value of ethnic medicine, and proposed that protection should shift from "quantity growth" to "quality improvement", and that a systematic and ecological protection and inheritance system should be constructed, providing theoretical basis and policy reference for the sustainable development of acupuncture and moxibustion intangible cultural heritage.

summary.question: 중국의 성급 이상 침구 무형문화유산 사업은 어떤 분포·구조적 특징을 보이며 보호상 어떤 과제가 있는가?

papers.title: [From fascial tension abnormality to myofascial chain: modern anatomical and biomechanical interpretation of "taking painful points as acupoints" in acupuncture and moxibustion].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Zhou D, Teng J, Xu J, Wang R, Luo W, Xu Y
papers.abstract: "Taking painful points as acupoints" is an important principle of acupoint selection in acupuncture and moxibustion. But its traditional connotation and modern mechanism have long been controversial. In this paper, the principle of "taking painful points as acupoints" is reinterpreted in light of anatomical and biomechanical studies of fascial system. Fascia, as a tension network covering the whole body, plays a crucial role in the onset and persistence of pain. The abnormal fascial tension may form tender points and myofascial trigger points (MTrPs), which are highly consistent with the distribution of ashi points. The continuity of myofascial chain can partially explain meridian pathways and distal effect of acupuncture and moxibustion in mechanistic studies. The mechanotransmission and mechanotransduction induced by acupuncture acting on the fascia-neural network provide a potential biological basis for deqi and analgesic effect. Based on the above understandings, this study further investigates the correlation between mechanical nature of ashi points, tender points and MTrPs in fascial tension field and their clinical practice, as well as the relationship of them with meridian pathways and distal effect. Therefore, it is concluded that "taking painful points as acupoints" not only represents the refinement of practical experience of acupuncture and moxibustion, but also serves as the surface mapping of abnormal fascial states. Such understanding provides new theoretical support for the transition from empirical acupoint selection to precise acupoint selection in acupuncture and moxibustion, and also expands new research and practical approaches for the comprehensive management of chronic pain.

summary.methods: 근막계의 해부학·생체역학 연구를 바탕으로 아시혈, 압통점, 근막 유발통증점의 관련성과 경락·원위 효과를 문헌적으로 재해석한 서술적 고찰이다.

papers.title: [WANG Hua's clinical experience in treating mammary gland hyperplasia with the "double consolidation and one unblocking" acupuncture method].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Mao J, Wang S, Wei Y, Wu S
papers.abstract: This article introduces Professor WANG Hua's clinical experience in treating mammary gland hyperplasia with the "double consolidation and one unblocking" acupuncture method. Professor WANG considers that deficiency of the spleen and kidney, disharmony of the Chong meridian and conception vessel, liver qi stagnation, and obstruction caused by phlegm-qi stagnation are the fundamental pathogenesis of this disease. Guided by the principle of "protecting healthy qi and treating diseases through prevention", Professor WANG applies the "double consolidation and one unblocking" acupuncture method, consolidating the congenital foundation (Guanyuan [CV4]) and acquired foundation (Zusanli [ST36]) to strengthen healthy qi, while emphasizing soothing the liver and regulating qi (Taichong [LR3]) and unblocking local lesions (ashi points or symptom-based selected points). Through precise acupoint selection, combined use of acupuncture and moxibustion, and simultaneous application of reinforcing and reducing methods, this approach nourishes the congenital foundation, strengthens the acquired foundation, and eliminates pathogenic factors, achieving favorable clinical outcomes in the treatment of mammary gland hyperplasia.

papers.title: [LIU Yue's clinical experience in treating peripheral facial paralysis with stage-based pattern differentiation acupuncture].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Shen Y, Ruan Q, Yang X, Zeng H, Ke M, Huang H et al.
papers.abstract: This article systematically summarizes Professor LIU Yue's clinical experience in treating peripheral facial paralysis using a stage-based pattern differentiation acupuncture approach. Professor LIU proposed a refined diagnostic and therapeutic model of "taking staging as the guiding principle and pathogenesis as the key point", which integrates traditional stage-based pattern differentiation with modern neuropathological mechanisms to achieve precise staging and pathogenesis differentiation. The treatment strategy includes stage-specific acupuncture techniques, including the contralateral needling method during the acute stage, penetrating acupuncture method during the recovery stage, and fire needle pricking method during the sequelae stage. It also incorporates an integrated application of characteristic techniques, including postauricular collateral bloodletting for reducing swelling and decompression, quantitative adjustment of penetrating acupuncture intensity according to the House-Brackmann facial nerve function grading system, and abdominal acupuncture for holistic regulation. Pattern-based acupuncture interventions are also applied, including fire needle combined with Wanhua oil rubbing manipulation to warm yang and unblock collaterals, yin-yang balancing acupuncture to improve muscle strength and correct abnormal facial movements, and dropping needling manipulation to relieve spasms and control synkinesis. Meanwhile, standardized operation procedures are emphasized to achieve the diagnostic and therapeutic goals of "staging, pathogenesis differentiation, technique selection, and standardization".

papers.title: [ZHUANG Lixing's experience of mind-regulating and pivot-restoring therapy in treatment of postural instability of Parkinson's disease].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Liao K, Fan J, Liu X, Han M, Zhuang L
papers.abstract: This paper summarizes Professor ZHUANG Lixing's clinical experience in treatment of postural instability in Parkinson's disease (PD) with acupuncture. The core pathogenesis of this disease lies in "imbalanced pivoting" of the governor vessel, Shaoyang meridians and the belt vessel. The pathological evolution follows the pattern of "loss of spirit/mind governance, loss of qi pivoting, and loss of physical function". The therapeutic principle is "mind-regulating, pivot-restoring, and sinew-relaxing", with the method of "mind-regulating and pivot-restoring" operated throughout treatment. The main acupoint prescriptions include "mind-regulating needling" (Sishenzhen, Shenting [GV24], Yintang [GV24+], Shenmen [HT7] Sanyinjiao [SP6]), "pivot-restoring acupoints" (Dusanzhen, Fengchi [GB20], Waiguan [TE5], Zulinqi [GB41]), and "the sinew-relaxing acupoints" (Yanglingquan [GB34], Luansanzhen, aishi point). Treatment is administered according to the stage of disease progression and the acupoints are modified based on symptoms, and the acupuncture technique of "directing qi to preserve essence", and fire needling are combined. This therapeutic idea emphasizes the integration of acupuncture and rehabilitation training, adopts staging treatment based on illness conditions, and demonstrates clear therapeutic effect. This therapeutic regimen can stabilize the central axis, correct gait, relieve contracture, improve motor function and enhance quality of life in PD patients with postural instability.

papers.title: [Effect of electroacupuncture at Jiaji (EX-B2) on disease progression in mice with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis based on NLRP3/Caspase-1/ASC signaling pathway].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Wang S, Wang M, Sun Y, Liu G, Li Y, Zhang W et al.
papers.abstract:
To explore the underlying mechanism of electroacupuncture (EA) at "Jiaji" (EX-B2) on the disease progression through modulating NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3)/cysteine-aspartic acid protease 1 (Caspase-1)/apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a caspase recruitment domain (ASC) signaling pathway in mice with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
Forty-five mice carrying the human superoxide dismutase 1 G93A (hSOD1G93A) gene were randomly divided into a model group, a Jiaji EA group, and an inhibitor group, 15 mice per group. The other 15 mice without hSOD1G93A gene carried were collected as a wild group. When the mice were aged 60 days, in the Jiaji EA group, EA was operated at "Jiaji" (EX-B2) of L1/L2, L5/L6, with continuous wave, a frequency of 2 Hz and an intensity of 1 mA, retained for 20 min, twice a week; in the inhibitor group, the intraperitoneal injection with NLRP3 inhibitor (10 mg/kg) was administered, twice a week. The interventions lasted for 4 weeks in each group. When the mice were aged 120 days, 9 mice in each group were randomly selected for tissue collection from lumbar spinal cord, and the disease progression and limb function were observed for the remaining 6 mice. The neurological function score was employed to assess the disease progression of mice in each group, and the gait experiment was conducted to observe the gait and stride length; HE staining was used to observe the motor neuron morphology in the anterior horn of the lumbar spinal cord, immunohistochemistry was used to detect the expression of ionic calcium-binding adapter molecule 1 (Iba-1) in the anterior horn of the lumbar spinal cord, and Western blot was used to detect the protein expression of NLRP3, Caspase-1, ASC, interleukin (IL)-18 and IL-1β in lumbar spinal cord.
Compared with the wild group, in the model group, the disease was worsened progressively, on days 90 and 120 after birth, the stride length of mice was reduced (P<0.05, P<0.01), and the gait was unstable and dragging on 120 days after birth; the motor neurons in the anterior horn of the spinal cord exhibited obvious cellular edema and rupture, marked vacuolization and nuclear pyknosis, along with severe neuron loss; the expression of Iba-1 increased in the anterior horn of the lumbar spinal cord (P<0.01), colored dark brown and densely aggregated; and the protein expression of NLRP3, Caspase-1, ASC, IL-18, IL-1β in lumbar spinal cord was up-regulated (P<0.01). When compared with the model group, in the inhibitor group and the Jiaji EA group, the onset of paresis and the progression of paralysis were delayed and the survival rates increased (P<0.01); stride length was larger in the mice at the age of 120 d (P<0.01); more clear gait was presented, and the ages in days was significantly delayed for gait dragging; the improvements were exhibited in the degree of edema, vacuolization, and nuclear pyknosis observed in the motor neurons of the anterior horn of the lumbar spinal cord; the expression of Iba-1 was reduced in the anterior horn of the lumbar spinal cord (P<0.01), appearing gray-brown, and scattered clusters in small number; and the protein expression of NLRP3, Caspase-1, ASC, IL-18, and IL-1β in lumbar spinal cord was decreased (P<0.05, P<0.01). The protein expression of NLRP3, Caspase-1 and IL-18 in lumbar spinal cord in the Jiaji EA group was up-regulated in comparison with that in the inhibitor group (P<0.05).
Electroacupuncture at "Jiaji" (EX-B2) can delay the disease progression in mice with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, which may be related to modulating NLRP3/Caspase-1/ASC signaling pathway and inhibiting the inflammatory response, thereby attenuating the inflammatory injury of lumbar spinal cord.

papers.title: [Effect of electroacupuncture on microglial activation in the spinal dorsal horn of rats with postherpetic neuralgia based on the BDNF/TrkB pathway].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Zhang R, Zou J
papers.abstract:
To observe the effects of electroacupuncture (EA) on the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)/tyrosine kinase receptor B (TrkB) pathway and microglial activation in the spinal dorsal horn of rats with postherpetic neuralgia (PHN).
Five of 20 male SD rats were randomly assigned to the normal control (NC) group, and the remaining rats received intraperitoneal injection of resiniferatoxin solution (200 μg/kg) to establish a PHN model. Successfully modeled rats were randomly divided into a PHN group, an EA group, and an EA+BDNF group, with 5 rats in each group. The rats in the EA group received EA at ashi points, "Xinshu" (BL15), and "Danshu" (BL19) on the left side, with disperse-dense wave (2 Hz/15 Hz) and a current intensity of 1 mA, 30 min per session, once daily for 4 consecutive weeks. In the EA+BDNF group, 10 μg of recombinant rat BDNF protein solution was administered by intrathecal injection before each EA treatment. The mechanical withdrawal threshold was assessed using Von Frey analgesia meter, and the thermal withdrawal latency was evaluated using plantar thermal stimulation apparatus. Immunofluorescence staining was used to detect the positive expression of ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule 1 (Iba-1), a marker of microglial activation, in the spinal dorsal horn. ELISA was used to measure interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) levels in the spinal dorsal horn. Western blot was used to detect the protein expression of BDNF and TrkB in the spinal dorsal horn.
Compared with the NC group, the PHN group showed decreased mechanical withdrawal threshold and increased thermal withdrawal latency (P<0.05), while positive Iba-1 expression, IL-1β and TNF-α levels, and BDNF and TrkB protein expression in the spinal dorsal horn were increased (P<0.05). Compared with the PHN group, the EA group showed increased mechanical withdrawal threshold and decreased thermal withdrawal latency (P<0.05), while positive Iba-1 expression, IL-1β and TNF-α levels, and BDNF and TrkB protein expression in the spinal dorsal horn were decreased (P<0.05). Compared with the EA+BDNF group, the EA group showed increased mechanical withdrawal threshold and decreased thermal withdrawal latency (P<0.05), while positive Iba-1 expression, IL-1β and TNF-α levels, and BDNF and TrkB protein expression in the spinal dorsal horn were all decreased (P<0.05).
EA could alleviate pain symptoms in rats with PHN, possibly by regulating the BDNF/TrkB pathway, inhibiting microglial activation in the spinal dorsal horn, and reducing inflammatory factor levels.

papers.title: [Effect of medicated-thread moxibustion of Zhuang medicine on autophagy in gastric smooth muscle cells of rats with diabetic gastroparesis via miR-10b-5p/PTEN/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Xu H, He Y, Wu Y, Wang Z, Zhang F, Fan Y
papers.abstract:
To investigate the underlying mechanism of medicated-thread moxibustion of Zhuang medicine in intervention of diabetic gastroparesis (DGP).
A total of 63 male SD rats were randomly divided into a blank group (13 rats) and a model preparation group (50 rats). The DGP models were established in the model preparation group by intraperitoneal injection of 1% streptozotocin (55 mg/kg). Forty successfully modeled rats were randomized into a model group, a western medicatione group, a non-meridian and non-point group, and a yangming meridian point group, with 10 rats in each group. In the yangming meridian point group, the medicated-thread moxibustion of Zhuang medicine was operated at bilateral "Liangmen" (ST21), "Qichong" (ST30), "Zusanli" (ST36), and "Fenglong" (ST40), with 3 moxa cones at each point. In the non-meridian and non-point group, the medicated-thread moxibustion of Zhuang medicine was operated at the sites not belonging to either meridian or meridian point, with 3 moxa cones per site. In the western medication group, mosapride citrate suspension was administered via gavage (10 mL/kg). All interventions were performed once daily, and for 3 consecutive weeks. Blood glucose level, gastric emptying rate, and small intestinal propulsion rate were measured in each group. HE staining was used to observe the morphology of gastric smooth muscle in gastric amooth muscle; Western blot was used to detect the protein expression of ubiquitin-bound protein p62 (p62), Beclin1, phosphatase-tensin homolog (PTEN), phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K), protein kinase B (AKT), microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 Ⅱ (LC3-Ⅱ) and microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3Ⅰ (LC3-Ⅰ) in gastric smooth muscle, and the ratio of LC3-Ⅱ/Ⅰ was calculated. Using the real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), the mRNA expression of microRNA-10b-5p (miR-10b-5p), PTEN, PI3K, and AKT was detected in gastric smooth muscle. With dual-luciferase reporter assay adopted, the targeting relationship between miR-10b-5p and PTEN was verified.
Compared with the blank group, the model group showed the increase in blood glucose level (P<0.05), the decrease in gastric emptying rate and small intestinal propulsion rate (P<0.05), disrupted and disorganized gastric smooth muscle cell structure, elevated protein expression of p62 and Beclin1 and LC3-Ⅱ/Ⅰ ratio (P<0.05), reduced mRNA expression of miR-10b-5p (P<0.05), higher protein and mRNA expression of PTEN (P<0.05), and lower protein and mRNA expression of PI3K and AKT (P<0.05). When compared with the model group, the Yangming meridian point group exhibited the decrease in blood glucose level (P<0.05); both the Yangming meridian point group and the western medication group showed the increase in gastric emptying rates and small intestinal propulsion rates (P<0.05), relatively intact gastric smooth muscle cell structure, reduced protein expression of p62 and Beclin1, and LC3-Ⅱ/Ⅰ ratio (P<0.05); higher mRNA expression of miR-10b-5p (P<0.05), lower protein and mRNA expression of PTEN (P<0.05) and higher protein and mRNA expression of PI3K and AKT (P<0.05). Compared with the non-meridian and non-point group, in the Yangming meridian point group, blood glucose decreased (P<0.05), gastric emptying rate and small intestinal propulsion rate increased (P<0.05), the structure of gastric smooth muscle cells was relatively intact, the protein expression of p62 and Beclin1 and LC3-Ⅱ/Ⅰ ratio were reduced (P<0.05); the mRNA expression of miR-10b-5p was elevated (P<0.05), the protein and mRNA expression of PTEN was reduced (P<0.05), and the protein and mRNA expression of PI3K and AKT rose (P<0.05). When the PTEN wild-type (PTEN-WT) fluorescent plasmid was co-transfected with miR-10b-5p mimics, the relative luciferase activity decreased (P<0.001).
The medicated-thread moxibustion of Zhuang medicine ameliorates the delayed gastric emptying in DGP rats, which may be related to its regulation of the miR-10b-5p/PTEN/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, thereby inhibiting autophagy in gastric smooth muscle cells.

papers.title: [Tiaoqi electroacupuncture alleviates chronic pain-depression comorbidity via miRNA-124- mediated JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Wang T, Yang P, Zhang X, Huang W, Li X, Huang X et al.
papers.abstract:
To observe the effects of Tiaoqi (regulating qi) electroacupuncture (EA) on the micro ribonucleic acid-124 (miRNA-124) and Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (JAK2/STAT3) signaling pathway in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) of rats with chronic pain-depression comorbidity (CPDC).
Sixty male SD rats were randomly divided into a blank group, a model group, an EA group and an EA+inhibitor group, with 15 rats in each group. Except for the blank group, the CPDC model was established by intraplantar injection of complete Freund's adjuvant in the other groups. Twenty-four hours after successful modeling, rats in the EA+inhibitor group received stereotaxic injection of miRNA-124 inhibitor into the PFC. Fourteen days after stereotaxic injection, Tiaoqi EA intervention was applied at bilateral "Hegu" (LI4) and "Taichong" (LR3) in the EA group and the EA+inhibitor group, with continuous wave, in frequency of 1.5 Hz, 20 min per time, once a day, for 14 consecutive days. Before modeling, after modeling and after intervention, mechanical withdrawal threshold (MWT) and thermal withdrawal latency (TWL) were adopted to evaluate pain-like behaviors; open field test (OFT), sucrose preference test (SPT) and forced swimming test (FST) were performed to evaluate depression- like behaviors. After intervention, the expression of miRNA-124 in the PFC was detected by real-time quantitative PCR; the positive expression of JAK2, p-JAK2, STAT3 and p-STAT3 in the PFC was detected by immunohistochemistry; the levels of oxidative stress-related factors i.e. malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT) and glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) in the PFC were detected by ELISA; the protein expression of apoptosis-related factors B-cell lymphoma-2 (Bcl-2), Bcl-2-associated X protein (Bax) and cleaved cysteinyl aspartate specific proteinase-3 (Cleaved-Caspase-3) in the PFC was detected by Western blot; the neuronal apoptosis rate in the PFC was measured by TUNEL staining; the neuronal morphology in the PFC tissue was observed by HE staining.
Compared with the blank group, the MWT, TWL, sucrose preference rate, total movement distance and central residence time of OFT were decreased (P<0.05), the immobility time of FST was prolonged (P<0.05) in the model group. Compared with the model group, the MWT, TWL, sucrose preference rate, total movement distance and central residence time of OFT were increased (P<0.05), the immobility time of FST was shortened (P<0.05) in the EA group. Compared with the EA+inhibitor group, the MWT, TWL, sucrose preference rate, total movement distance and central residence time of OFT were increased (P<0.05), the immobility time of FST was shortened (P<0.05) in the EA group. Compared with the blank group, in the model group, the expression of miRNA-124, levels of SOD, CAT and GSH-Px, and protein expression of Bcl-2 in the PFC were decreased (P<0.05); the positive expression of p-JAK2 and p-STAT3, level of MDA, protein expression of Bax and Cleaved-Caspase-3, Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, and neuronal apoptosis rate were increased (P<0.05); the PFC neurons showed disordered arrangement, vacuoles and neurofibrillary tangles could be observed in the tissue interstitium, a large number of neurons exhibited pyknosis and hyperchromasia, and pyramidal cells were decreased or even disappeared. Compared with the model group, in the EA group, the expression of miRNA-124, levels of SOD, CAT and GSH-Px, and protein expression of Bcl-2 were increased in the PFC (P<0.05); the positive expression of p-JAK2 and p-STAT3, level of MDA, the protein expression of Bax and Cleaved-Caspase-3, Bax/Bcl-2 ratio and neuronal apoptosis rate were reduced (P<0.05); only a small number of pyknotic neurons were observed in the PFC tissue, with narrowed tissue interstitium and increased pyramidal cells. All the above indexes were improved in the EA group compared with those in the EA+inhibitor group.
Tiaoqi EA can effectively relieve CPDC by regulating the miRNA-124-mediated JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway, alleviating oxidative stress and inhibiting neuronal apoptosis.

summary.question: 기치 조절 전침이 만성 통증-우울 공병의 행동학적 이상과 PFC의 분자 표지자를 개선하는지 평가하였다.

papers.title: [Acupuncture regulates the Th17/Treg axis for chronic spontaneous urticaria: a randomized controlled trial].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Guo J, Yang L, He L, Yang Z, Zhu Y, Shi H
papers.abstract:
To observe the clinical efficacy of acupuncture for chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) and its effect on the helper T cell 17(Th17)/regulatory T cell (Treg) axis.
Eighty CSU patients were randomly divided into an observation group (40 cases, 2 cases dropped out) and a control group (40 cases, 2 cases dropped out). The observation group received acupuncture at bilateral Jianyu (LI15), Shousanli (LI10), Quchi (LI11), Pianli (LI6), Xuehai (SP10), Zusanli (ST36) and Sanyinjiao (SP6), each session lasting for 30 min, 3 times per week. The control group received oral ebastine tablets, 10 mg each time, once daily. Both groups were treated for 8 weeks. The 7-day urticaria activity score (UAS7), dermatology life quality index (DLQI) score and Hamilton anxiety scale (HAMA) score were observed, peripheral blood Th17 and Treg cell proportions, and serum levels of interleukin (IL)-17, IL-23, IL-10, and IL-35 were detected, and the ratio of Th17/Treg was calculated before and after treatment in the two groups.
After treatment, the UAS7, DLQI and HAMA scores in the two groups were decreased compared with those before treatment (P<0.05), and the scores in the observation group were lower than those in the control group (P<0.05). After treatment, the peripheral blood Th17 cell proportions, the ratios of Th17/Treg and serum levels of IL-17, IL-23 in the two groups were decreased compared with those before treatment (P<0.05), those indexes in the observation group were lower than those in the control group (P<0.05). After treatment, the peripheral blood Treg cell proportions, and serum levels of IL-10, IL-35 in the two groups were increased compared with those before treatment (P<0.05), those indexes in the observation group were higher than those in the control group (P<0.05).
Acupuncture can effectively alleviate the symptoms of CSU, and its mechanism of action may be related to the regulation of the Th17/Treg axis.
papers.title_ko: 침치료가 만성 자발성 두드러기의 Th17/Treg 축을 조절하는가: 무작위 대조시험

summary.question: 침치료가 만성 자발성 두드러기(CSU)의 임상 증상과 Th17/Treg 축에 영향을 주는지 평가하였다.
summary.methods: CSU 환자를 침치료군과 에바스틴 복용 대조군으로 무작위 배정해 8주간 비교한 무작위 대조시험이다.
summary.results: 침치료군은 UAS7, DLQI, HAMA와 Th17/Treg 관련 염증 지표가 더 크게 감소하고 Treg 및 항염증성 사이토카인이 더 크게 증가하였다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: CSU에서 침치료가 증상과 일부 면역지표를 개선할 수 있으나, 기전 해석은 대조약물과 단기 결과에 근거한 것으로 보아야 한다.
summary.limitations: 단일 비교약물과 8주 추적의 단기 연구라 장기 효과와 일반화 가능성은 제한적이다.

pico.o: UAS7, DLQI, HAMA 및 Th17/Treg 관련 면역지표 변화

papers.title: [Skin resistance measurement in chronic gastrointestinal disorders and its correlation with visceral referred pain].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Rao X, Liu K, He X, Gao X, Cui X, Zhu B
papers.abstract:
To observe the body surface reaction points in patients with chronic gastrointestinal disorders, and analyze the correlation between their resistance values and the severity of visceral referred pain.
A total of 103 patients with chronic gastritis and 38 patients with inflammatory bowel disease were enrolled in the clinical study, and were subsequently divided into three groups based on the severity of visceral referred pain, including a mild pain group, a moderate pain group, and a severe pain group. The finger-pressure method was employed to perform exploratory palpation over the trunk and extremities, so as to identify reaction points and control points, as well as observe the distribution of these reaction points; and they were subsequently marked on the human nerve dermatome distribution map. Using a meridian and acupoint dynamic characteristic analyzer, the resistance values at the reaction points and control points were measured, and the correlation was analyzed between the resistance change rate and the severity of visceral referred pain.
In the patients with chronic gastritis, the reaction points were primarily distributed in the T8 to T9 nerve segments on the right, whereas in the patients with inflammatory bowel disease, the reaction points were predominantly concentrated in the T10 to T12 nerve segments on the right. Patients with chronic gastritis and inflammatory bowel disease exhibited lower resistance values at the reaction points compared with the control points (P<0.05). The resistance values at control points in the severe pain group were lower than those in the mild pain group (P<0.05), and the resistance change rate in both the moderate pain group and the severe pain group was higher than that in the mild pain group (P<0.05). The resistance change rate in female patients was positively correlated with the severity of visceral referred pain (P<0.01).
The reaction points of chronic gastrointestinal disorders are primarily distributed at the body surface sites innervated by the nerve segments corresponding to their respective organs, and these reaction points exhibit reduced resistance, and the resistance change rate at these reaction points can be utilized to distinguish between mild and severe pain.
papers.title_ko: 만성 위장관 질환에서 피부 저항 측정과 내장 연관통의 상관성

summary.question: 만성 위장관 질환 환자의 체표 반응점 저항값이 내장 연관통의 중증도와 관련되는지 평가하였다.
summary.methods: 만성 위염 103명과 염증성 장질환 38명을 대상으로 반응점과 대조점을 촉진·표지하고, 경락·경혈 동특성 분석기로 저항값과 저항 변화율을 측정해 연관통 중증도와의 상관을 분석한 임상연구이다.
summary.results: 반응점은 해당 장기와 대응하는 신경절 분절에 주로 분포했으며 저항값은 대조점보다 낮았고, 저항 변화율은 중등도·중증군에서 경증군보다 높아 통증 중증도 구분과 관련되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 연구는 만성 위장관 질환에서 체표 반응점의 저항 변화가 내장 연관통의 중증도와 연관될 수 있음을 시사하지만, 임상 적용 전 추가 검증이 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 관찰연구로서 인과관계를 확정할 수 없고, 질환군과 성별에 따른 해석에 주의가 필요하다.

papers.title: [Herbal cake-separated moxibustion combined with Bufei Tongluo decoction in treatment of diabetes-induced pulmonary fibrosis of qi-yin deficiency with blood stagnation: a randomized controlled trial].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Zeng X, Wang G, Yang Q, Zhang D, Liang S, Shen H
papers.abstract:
To observe the clinical efficacy of herbal cake-separated moxibustion combined with Bufei Tongluo decoction on diabetes-induced pulmonary fibrosis (DiPF) of qi-yin deficiency with blood stagnation.
A total of 102 DiPF patients were randomly divided into an observation group (51 cases, 1 case dropped out) and a control group (51 cases, 1 case was eliminated and 1 case dropped out). In the control group, Bufei Tongluo decoction was administered, one dose per day; and in the observation group, herbal cake-separated moxibustion was operated at Danzhong (CV17) and bilateral Feishu (BL13), Gaohuang (BL43), Zusanli (ST36), etc. on the basis of the treatment in the control group, once every two days, three times a week. The interventions in the two groups were operated continuously for 8 weeks. The TCM symptom score, high-resolution CT (HRCT) score, the 6-minute walk test (6MWT), the indexes of pulmonary function test (the percentage of measured values of the total lung capacity [TLC], forced vital capacity [FVC], and lung carbon monoxide diffusion capacity [DLCO] relative to predicted values), and the levels of serological markers (hydroxyproline [Hyp], interleukin-10 [IL-10] and transforming growth factor-β [TGF-β]) were compared before and after treatment in the twogroups. The clinical efficacy and safety of both groups were evaluated.
After treatment, the scores of each symptom (dry cough with little phlegm, shortness of breath and fatigue, dry mouth and throat, feverish sensations in the palms and soles, and stabbing pain in the chest and hypochondriac region) and the total scores of TCM syndrome, HRCT scores, and the levels of serum Hyp, IL-10, and TGF-β in both groups decreased in comparison with those before treatment (P<0.05); and the scores of dry cough with little phlegm, shortness of breath and fatigue, stabbing pain in the chest and hypochondriac region, the total score of TCM syndrome, HRCT score, the levels of serum IL-10 and TGF-β in the observation group were lower than those in the control group (P<0.05). After treatment, the 6MWT and the percentages of measured values of TLC, FVC and DLCO relative to predicted values in both groups increased in comparison with those before treatment (P<0.05); and the percentages of measured values of TLC, FVC and DLCO relative to predicted values in the observation group were higher than those in the control group (P<0.05). The clinical efficacy of the observation group was superior to the control group (P<0.05). The total effective rate in the observation group was 98.0% (49/50), without statistically significant difference compared with the control group (87.8% [43/49], P>0.05). There was no statistically significant difference in the incidence of adverse reactions between the two groups (P>0.05).
Herbal cake-separated moxibustion combined with Bufei Tongluo decoction can effectively alleviate clinical symptoms, improve pulmonary function, and reduce inflammatory response and fibrosis in DiPF patients of qi-yin deficiency with blood stagnation.
papers.title_ko: 허브 떡분리뜸과 보폐통락탕 병용의 당뇨병 유발 폐섬유화 치료: 무작위 대조시험

summary.question: 기(氣)·음(陰) 부족과 혈어(血瘀)를 동반한 당뇨병 유발 폐섬유화에서 허브 떡분리뜸에 보폐통락탕을 병용하는 것이 증상을 개선하는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: 당뇨병 유발 폐섬유화 환자를 무작위로 나누어 대조군은 보폐통락탕만, 관찰군은 여기에 허브 떡분리뜸을 8주간 병행한 무작위 대조시험이다.
summary.results: 병용군은 한약 단독군보다 일부 증상, HRCT 점수, IL-10과 TGF-β, 그리고 폐기능 지표가 더 많이 개선되었고, 이상반응 차이는 없었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 연구는 뜸과 한약 병용이 특정 변증의 당뇨병 유발 폐섬유화에서 증상과 검사 지표 개선과 연관될 수 있음을 시사하지만, 단일 연구 결과로 일반화에는 주의가 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 단일 연구이며 변증 기반 대상자와 단기 추적에 국한되어 있어 효과의 지속성과 재현성은 추가 연구가 필요하다.

papers.title: [Tiaoshen acupuncture for shift work circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder: a randomized controlled trial].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Xu W, Wang C, Chen Y, Jiang S, Xu F, Pan X
papers.abstract:
To observe the clinical efficacy of Tiaoshen (regulating the mind) acupuncture for shift work circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder (SWD).
A total of 84 patients with shift work circadian rhythm SWD were randomly divided into a Tiaoshen acupuncture group (42 cases, 1 case dropped out) and a non-meridian non-acupoint group (42 cases, 2 cases dropped out). Both groups received sleep health education as basic treatment. The Tiaoshen acupuncture group was treated with Tiaoshen acupuncture, Baihui (GV20), bilateral Fengchi (GB20), Touwei (ST8), Shenmen (HT7), Zusanli (ST36), as well as auricular points Shenmen (TF4), Xin (CO15) were selected. The non-meridian non-acupoint group received shallow needling at non-meridian non-acupoint points, as well as non-related auricular points. Both groups were treated 3 times per week for 4 weeks. Before treatment, after treatment, and after 3 months of treatment completion, the morningness-eveningness questionnaire (MEQ), Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI), self-rating anxiety scale (SAS), and self-rating depression scale (SDS) were used to assess the sleep and emotional status in the two groups.
Compared before treatment, the MEQ scores were increased after treatment and after 3 months of treatment completion in the two groups (P<0.001, P<0.01); the scores of PSQI, SAS and SDS were decreased after treatment and after 3 months of treatment completion in the Tiaoshen acupuncture group (P<0.001), and the scores of SAS and SDS were decreased after treatment in the non-meridian non-acupoint group (P<0.01). After treatment and after 3 months of treatment completion, the MEQ scores in the Tiaoshen acupuncture group were higher than those in the non-meridian non-acupoint group (P<0.001), and the PSQI scores in the Tiaoshen acupuncture group were lower than those in the non-meridian non-acupoint group (P<0.001); after treatment, the SAS and SDS scores in the Tiaoshen acupuncture group were lower than those in the non-meridian non-acupoint group (P<0.05, P<0.01).
Tiaoshen acupuncture can effectively improve the sleep-wake rhythm and sleep quality of patients with shift work circadian rhythm SWD, alleviate the accompanying anxiety and depression.
papers.title_ko: 교신(調神) 침법이 교대근무 일주기성 수면-각성장애에 미치는 효과: 무작위대조시험

summary.question: 교대근무 일주기성 수면-각성장애에서 교신 침법이 수면-각성 리듬과 수면·정서 상태를 개선하는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: 84명의 환자를 교신 침법군과 비경락 비혈위 대조군으로 무작위 배정하고, 양군 모두 수면보건교육을 시행한 뒤 4주간 침 치료 전후와 3개월 추적에서 MEQ, PSQI, SAS, SDS를 비교했다.
summary.results: 교신 침법군은 대조군보다 MEQ와 PSQI가 더 크게 개선되고 SAS, SDS도 더 많이 감소했으며, 효과는 치료 후와 3개월 추적에서 유지되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 이 연구는 교대근무 관련 수면-각성장애에서 교신 침법이 수면 리듬과 수면의 질, 불안·우울 지표를 개선할 가능성을 시사하지만, 근거는 단일 RCT 결과로 해석해야 한다.

papers.title: [Beyond the placebo effect: exploring the mast cell-dependent analgesic effect of shallow needling control].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Luo Z, Zhang Y, Ge X, Tian X, Zhang L, Nie J et al.
papers.abstract: Based on the distribution characteristics of mast cells and existing mechanistic evidence, the study explores the potential biological effects of shallow needling control (sham-acupuncture). Regarding cellular distribution, mast cells exhibit a physiological characteristic of dense distribution in both the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, predominantly in the distal regions, and show a higher density in acupoint areas compared with non-acupoint areas. At the puncture site, shallow needling primarily targets the dermis and the superficial subcutaneous tissue, with these two layers overlapping anatomically. Regarding its mechanism of action, acupuncture can induce local mast cell degranulation through mechanical stimulation, thereby releasing bioactive substances that subsequently activate relevant signaling pathways to produce analgesic effect. The study proposes that the shallow needling control at the same acupoint or non-acupoint not merely obtains placebo effect, but also involves potential biological mechanism associated with mast cells, aiming to provide new insights for future clinical trial design and research on the underlying mechanism of acupuncture and sham-acupuncture.
papers.title_ko: 위약 효과를 넘어서: 얕은 자침 대조의 비만세포 의존적 진통 효과 탐구

summary.question: 얕은 자침 대조가 단순 위약이 아니라 비만세포 관련 생물학적 진통 기전을 가질 수 있는지를 검토한 연구이다.
summary.methods: 비만세포의 분포 특성과 기존 기전 근거를 바탕으로 얕은 자침 대조의 생물학적 효과를 고찰한 기전 중심의 임상 연구이다.
summary.results: 얕은 자침은 진피와 표층 피하조직을 자극해 비만세포 탈과립과 관련 신호전달을 통해 진통 효과를 낼 가능성이 제시되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 침구 임상시험에서 얕은 자침 대조는 완전한 비활성 위약이 아닐 수 있어 대조군 해석에 주의가 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 실제 환자 대상의 효과 크기나 임상적 유효성을 직접 검증한 데이터가 아니라 기전적 고찰이라는 점이 한계이다.

papers.title: [Optimizing the clinical translation of acupuncture for the prevention and treatment of tumor-related complications based on implementation science].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Guo Z, Hu X, Tian Z, Chen H, Wang X, Xiu W et al.
papers.abstract: Acupuncture is an internationally recognized complementary approach in comprehensive tumor treatment. To address the bottleneck in its clinical translation in the prevention and treatment of tumor-related complications, this study, based on the concept of implementation science, proposes three core pathways and directions for future development. First, to construct a characteristic implementation framework of "general modules+acupuncture sub-modules", incorporating core elements of acupuncture such as syndrome differentiation and acupoint compatibility, as well as optional modules such as scenario adaptation and adjustment for special populations; second, to deepen the integration of medicine and engineering, and develop a standardized big data platform for acupuncture and intelligent monitoring and intervention devices adapted to primary care settings; third, to implement a hierarchical promotion system of "tertiary hospitals tackling key problems-community hospitals undertaking follow-up-home settings providing supplementation", and to improve skills training and safety quality control. These measures will promote the standardized and regulated development of acupuncture in the prevention and treatment of tumor-related complications, and provide strong support for reducing patient suffering and achieving the cancer prevention and control goals of "Healthy China 2030".

papers.title: [Analysis of influencing factors and evaluation methods for intervention fidelity in acupuncture clinical trials].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Wang L, Hu X, Gang W, Jing X
papers.abstract:
To systematically review and analyze the influencing factors and evaluation methods of intervention fidelity in acupuncture clinical trials, so as to provide a reference for constructing an evaluation framework of fidelity in acupuncture trials.
A computerized search was conducted on the influencing factors and evaluation methods of intervention fidelity in acupuncture clinical trials across CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, SinoMed, PubMed, EMbase, Cochrane Library databases, spanned from inception to December 31, 2025; and supplemented by manual retrieval for the references of included articles. Influencing factors were categorized using the updated consolidated framework for implementation research (CFIR), while evaluation content of the fidelity was summarized in accordance with the items from the standards for reporting interventions in clinical trials of acupuncture (STRICTA).
A total of 143 articles were included. Factors influencing acupuncture intervention fidelity included 5 categories, named acupuncture-specific attributes, external factors, internal factors, individual characteristics, and implementation processes. The most common factors were perceived efficacy of acupuncture (16 articles, 11.19%), complexity of acupuncture (11 articles, 7.69%), doctor-patient communication (9 articles, 6.29%), acupuncturist competence (13 articles, 9.09%), patient's attitude toward acupuncture (13 articles, 9.09%), and convenience of receiving treatment (16 articles, 11.19%). Fidelity evaluation aimed at therapy assessment, with subjects as the main targets; and evaluation dimensions covered 4 categories (pre-intervention preparation, needling details, treatment protocol, and supportive measures), encompassing 21 items. Multiple evaluation approaches, tools, standards, and time points were applied; and the evaluation results were primarily based on quantitative analysis, with partial incorporation of qualitative analysis. Most trials reported only the aforementioned evaluation components.
Key factors affecting acupuncture intervention fidelity include the acupuncture-specific attributes, doctor-patient communication, acupuncturist competence, patient attitudes, and treatment accessibility. Current fidelity evaluation methods in acupuncture trials are not unified and lack systematic assessment. In the future, a comprehensive and systematic fidelity evaluation methodology should be established to provide guidance for assessing the fidelity of acupuncture intervention.

papers.title: [Target trial emulation in acupuncture-moxibustion clinical research: from real-world data to causal inference].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Xu Z, Song S, Yu H, Wu S, Xu F, Shen Y et al.
papers.abstract: In order to elucidate the application value and implementation pathway of target trial emulation (TTE) in clinical research of acupuncture and moxibustion, this article reviews the key methodological components of TTE, including data readiness assessment, target trial protocol specification, treatment strategy allocation, alignment of time zero (T0), definition of outcomes and follow-up, estimation-based target choice, control of confounding and censoring, diagnostic and sensitivity analyses, and reporting standards. Key operational points are also summarized based on real-world study (RWS) cases of acupuncture and moxibustion. Using a hypothetical randomized controlled trial (RCT) as the reference, TTE translates a research question into an executable observational study protocol, thereby helping to address pre-control design bias, enhance research transparency and strengthen causal interpretation. The application of TTE in acupuncture- moxibustion research should rely on standardized case registration system and emphasize the structured collection of real-world data. Findings from TTE studies may serve as an important complement to RCT evidence, but they remain the limitations such as data quality, unmeasured confounding factors, and the difficulty in simulating sham-acupuncture controls. Hence, these findings should be interpreted and applied with caution.

papers.title: [Methodological exploration of embedding qualitative and mixed methods research in acupuncture pilot trials from the perspective of complex interventions].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Yu C, Liang S, Wang H, Shao H, Sun Y
papers.abstract: Large randomized controlled trials evaluating the efficacy of acupuncture often face challenges of high heterogeneity in outcomes. The underlying reason is that acupuncture, as a complex intervention, is simplified to a single intervention, while pilot trials fail to effectively optimize trial designs. Based on the framework of complex interventions, this article proposes a paradigm shift for acupuncture pilot trials, transforming them from simple quantitative feasibility assessments into comprehensive platforms for systematically improving the maturity of population, intervention, comparison, and outcome (PICO) elements. This article systematically reviews the necessity of embedding qualitative research or mixed methods research within this paradigm and elucidates their key roles in identifying core issues, optimizing interventions, refining procedures, exploring mechanisms, and enhancing the interpretability of results. Furthermore, mixed methods design strategies and specific implementation pathways tailored to different objectives are proposed. Finally, the challenges of this paradigm in terms of cognitive acceptance, methodological integration, and resource requirements, as well as corresponding strategies, are critically analyzed. This article aims to provide theoretical foundations and practical guidance for establishing a more rigorous and highly interpretable methodological framework for acupuncture clinical trials.

papers.title: [Interpretation of reporting standards for acupuncture clinical trials based on the CONSORT 2025 statement].
papers.journal: Zhongguo zhen jiu = Chinese acupuncture & moxibustion
papers.authors: Han F, Zuo J, Zhou T, Hu J
papers.abstract: Based on the consolidated standards of reporting trials (CONSORT) 2025 statement, the article introduces the interpretation and reporting examples of 9 key items that require special attention when conducting acupuncture randomized controlled trials (RCTs). The selected items cover patient and public involvement (item 8), eligibility criteria (item 12), intervention and control (items 13 and 24), outcomes (item 14), adverse events (items 15 and 27), sample size (item 16), and blinding (item 20). The article first elucidates the core reporting requirements of these items, and analyzes in detail the specific considerations and reporting points associated with the application of acupuncture RCTs in terms of the complexity of acupuncture interventions, the unique design of control groups, and the high operator-dependence of treatment delivery. Additionally, it demonstrates standardized reporting methods for each item by taking acupuncture RCTs published domestically and internationally in recent years as examples. The article aims to provide acupuncture researchers with specific and actionable reporting guidelines, thereby enhancing the credibility and clinical translational value of acupuncture research findings.

papers.title: The ameliorative effect of active ingredients of traditional Chinese medicine on male reproductive injury: A review.
papers.journal: Journal of ethnopharmacology
papers.authors: Tang X, Li C
papers.abstract:
Due to their unique advantages of multi-target synergy and holistic regulation, traditional Chinese medicines (TCM) show promising clinical applications in enhancing male reproductive function. The 'Qianjin Fang' and 'Compendium of Materia Medica' document the use of Wuzhi Yanzong Wan, Cistanche, Cuscuta, and Epimedium for over a thousand years in the preservation of male reproductive health.
This article provides a systematic review of research progress on the use of active components in TCM (including flavonoids, polyphenols, terpenoids, alkaloids, and polysaccharides) and related formulas in improving male reproductive damage. These compounds improve male fertility by regulating multiple signaling pathways. Furthermore, this review outlines future research directions and potential applications in this field, aiming to lay a theoretical foundation for the clinical treatment of male reproductive health using TCM and the development of novel therapeutic interventions.
The relevant literature on the effects of active ingredients in TCM and related formulas on improving male reproductive damage was retrieved from multiple databases, including Web of Science, ScienceDirect, PubMed, etc. RESULTS: Active components of TCM (such as icariin, hypericin, and quercetin) and their compound formulations (such as Guilu Erxian Jiao and Wuziyan Zongwan) can improve male reproductive damage by modulating core pathological cascades-including oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and endocrine disruption-and restoring the physiological microenvironment essential for normal spermatogenesis.
Extensive experiments have been performed to investigate the effects of active ingredients and herbal formulas on improving male reproductive dysfunction, revealing that TCM has the potential to combat male reproductive dysfunction through multi-level, multi-target mechanisms. However, there is a lack of reviews addressing the causes of male reproductive dysfunction and related treatment approaches. Therefore, this review aims to summarize current research progress in the use of TCM to combat male reproductive dysfunction, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for future preclinical validation and clinical application in the treatment of male reproductive dysfunction.

papers.title: Si-Shen-San Attenuates Alzheimer's Disease Pathology and Cognitive Deficits Through Multi-Target Regulation of Astrocyte Function and Synaptic Plasticity.
papers.journal: Journal of ethnopharmacology
papers.authors: Li Y, Tang ZL, Liu FW, Chen M, Chang SQ, Ding FM et al.
papers.abstract:
Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder pathologically characterized by cognitive decline, amyloid-β (Aβ) deposition, tau hyperphosphorylation, synaptic dysfunction, and astrocyte dysregulation. The constituent herbs of the traditional Chinese medicine formula Si-Shen-San (SSS) have been used to ameliorate cognitive impairment. However, the comprehensive chemical profile, core bioactive constituents, and underlying mechanisms of action of SSS remain to be fully elucidated.
This study aims to systematically investigate the therapeutic potential of SSS against AD and to clarify its multi-faceted mechanisms of action, with a focus on astrocyte-mediated neuroprotection, synaptic repair, and modulation of core AD pathologies.
Ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole/time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Q/TOF-MS) was used to characterize the chemical constituents of SSS extract and SSS-containing serum. In vivo, 3×Tg-AD mice were orally administered SSS. And cognitive function, AD-related pathology, synaptic integrity, and astrocyte-associated molecular changes were evaluated using behavioral, histological, biochemical, ultrastructural, and electrophysiological approaches. In vitro, an astrocyte-conditioned medium paradigm was used to examine whether SSS-induced changes in astrocytes were associated with protection of HT22 neurons against glutamate-induced injury.
UHPLC-Q/TOF-MS tentatively annotated 525 and 318 compounds in the SSS extract and drug-containing serum. In 3×Tg-AD mice, SSS improved cognitive performance, reduced hippocampal 6E10- and ThS-positive Aβ-like immunoreactivity and tau phosphorylation at Thr231 and Ser404, and preserved synaptic structure and function. The reduction in tau phosphorylation was accompanied by changes in GSK-3β signaling. SSS treatment was also associated with reduced astrocyte reactivity, increased GLT-1 expression, and restoration of astrocyte-associated homeostatic markers. In vitro, conditioned medium derived from SSS-treated C8-D1A astrocytes alleviated glutamate-induced injury in HT22 neurons and was accompanied by activation of neuronal CREB-BDNF signaling.
SSS ameliorated cognitive deficits and multiple AD-related pathological alterations in 3×Tg-AD mice. These effects were associated with restoration of astrocyte-related homeostatic features, improved glutamate regulation, preservation of synaptic integrity, and activation of CREB-BDNF signaling. These findings provide an experimental foundation for SSS as a potential therapeutic strategy for AD and highlight astrocyte homeostasis as a promising target for future drug development.

papers.title: Jingfang Baidu San Alleviates Feng-Han (Wind-Cold) Syndrome-Associated Lung Injury in Mice Through Macrophage Functional Regulation and Dectin-1-Associated Immune Remodeling.
papers.journal: Journal of ethnopharmacology
papers.authors: Zhou K, Gu M, Liu X, Yang L, Yan G, Sun H et al.
papers.abstract:
Jingfang Baidu San (JF) is a classic traditional Chinese medicine(TCM)formula that has been widely used in clinical practice for hundreds of years. While its efficacy in treating Feng Han (wind-cold, FH) common cold has garnered increasing attention, its underlying mechanism of action remain incompletely understood.
This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effect of JF on wind-cold common cold and to elucidate its molecular mechanism.
A mouse model of wind-cold syndrome (FH) was established by exposing mice to wind and cold stress for 7 consecutive days. The therapeutic effects of orally administered JF were initially evaluated by assessing behavioral manifestations, body weight, and rectal temperature. Lung histopathology was subsequently examined using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining. To investigate the potential molecular mechanisms underlying the effects of JF on FH, transcriptomic sequencing of lung tissues was performed to identify key differentially expressed genes and associated regulatory networks. Inflammatory cytokine levels in serum and lung tissues were further quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA), while the expression and localization of key molecular targets and related proteins were validated by immunofluorescence staining, immunohistochemistry, and Western blotting.
JF significantly ameliorated the major pathological manifestations in FH model mice, as evidenced by body weight recovery, reduction of elevated rectal temperature, and improvement of behavioral abnormalities including lethargy, hypoactivity, and respiratory abnormalities. Histopathological analysis further confirmed that JF markedly alleviated lung tissue injury and reduced the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6, IL-1β, and TNF-α in serum and lung tissue. At the mechanistic level, through transcriptomic analysis combined with in vivo validation, we identified Dectin-1 Clec7a as a potential macrophage-related regulatory node associated with the efficacy of JF in treating FH. JF treatment restored the expression of macrophage-associated Dectin-1, while attenuating macrophage-associated inflammatory responses and tissue remodeling responses. In conclusion, the protective effect of JF against FH-related lung injury is associated with the regulation of macrophage Dectin-1, inhibition of NF-κB activation, and attenuation of TGF-β-related responses, inflammatory responses, and abnormal extracellular matrix remodeling.
The protective effects of JF against FH-induced lung injury were associated with modulation of macrophage Dectin-1 expression, suppression of NF-κB activation, and attenuation of TGF-β-related signaling, accompanied by reduced inflammation and amelioration of aberrant extracellular matrix remodeling. These findings suggest that Dectin-1-mediated macrophage regulation may contribute to the protective effects of JF. Further genetic and pharmacological studies are needed to establish the causal roles of Dectin-1, NF-κB, and TGF-β-related signaling pathways in mediating the effects of JF.

papers.title: Emerging Applications of Scrophularia striata in Healthcare: A Scoping Review for Nursing Care.
papers.journal: Iranian journal of nursing and midwifery research
papers.authors: Nouri A, Khazaee A, Arkavaz RL, Bahalou M, Nouri R
papers.abstract:
Complementary therapy, such as herbal medicine, is one of the basic principles of nursing care and plays an important role in providing comprehensive care. The present scoping review aims to investigate the relevant evidence regarding the efficacy of Scrophularia striata in nursing practice, identify the major research areas, and recognize the knowledge gap to improve future studies.
The six-step methodological framework of Arksey and O'Malley was used in the present scoping review. A total of 1155 studies were retrieved from domestic and international databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library). Sixty-nine of these studies were analyzed after applying the exclusion criteria. Data extraction was performed independently by two reviewers. The synthesis involved analyzing recurring key themes across the studies to map and describe the included literature.
The analyzed studies revealed that the effects of S. striata on healthcare outcomes are divided into the following five groups: (1) antimicrobial effect, (2) antioxidant effect, (3) analgesic and anti-inflammatory effect, (4) neuroprotective and anti-anxiety effect, and (5) wound healing effect. A few studies have investigated the anti-nephrotoxic activity, antidiabetic, anti-asthmatic, and protective effects, which have been classified as other categories.
A small number of studies investigated the clinical efficacy and safety of S. striata. Thus, it is recommended to conduct more clinical trials on the efficacy of S. striata. The results of these studies can have an impact on holistic nursing practice as an adjunct treatment alongside routine nursing care.

papers.title: Efficacy of auriculotherapy in reducing pain: a comprehensive literature review.
papers.journal: Frontiers in pain research (Lausanne, Switzerland)
papers.authors: Faria M, Sargento P, Dias-Teixeira M, Maia E, Maia J, Pereira JP
papers.abstract:
This review examines the efficacy of auriculotherapy in reducing pain across acute and chronic contexts, focusing on pain intensity scores, analgesic requirements, and safety profiles.
A comprehensive, English-language literature search was conducted across PubMed, b-On, Web of Science, Scopus, and SciELO using Boolean combinations of terms related to auriculotherapy, chronic and acute pain, and randomized trials (searches first run March 2026, re-run June 2026). Eligibility was defined a priori using a PICOS framework. From 280 initially identified records, 13 studies were included after duplicate removal and eligibility screening, and findings were synthesized narratively by pain type given substantial heterogeneity across designs. Methodological quality was assessed using the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for the seven included primary RCTs and AMSTAR-2 for the five included systematic reviews/meta-analyses.
Auriculotherapy significantly reduced acute postoperative pain, with meta-analyzed Visual Analog Scale (VAS) reductions of -0.44 (95% CI: -0.72 to -0.17) at 24 h and an analgesic-requirement standardized mean difference of -0.88 (95% CI: -1.29 to -0.46). For chronic back pain, standardized mean differences ranged from -0.65 to -0.85. In migraine, VAS decreased by -0.65 (95% CI: -0.86 to -0.43) with attack frequency reduced by an MD of -0.49 (95% CI: -0.59 to -0.40). Cancer pain studies reported 36% VAS reductions at 2 months. Adverse events were minimal, limited to mild local reactions in less than 5%-8% of cases, with no serious events reported.
Auriculotherapy demonstrates moderate, consistent efficacy across pain types, likely mediated through autonomic modulation and endorphin release via somatotopic ear projections. A dose-response pattern emerged, with multiple sessions (2-3 weekly over 4-8 weeks) yielding sustained effects. Stronger benefits were observed in orthopedic perioperative settings and with needle-retention protocols. It concludes that auriculotherapy is a safe, viable non-pharmacological adjunct for pain management, while calling for large, diverse, standardized RCTs with longer follow-up and objective biomarker measures to strengthen the evidence base. Because these findings derive from a narrative synthesis of a heterogeneous mix of primary trials, they should be interpreted as indicative rather than definitive, particularly given the diversity of study designs and predominantly Asian/perioperative populations represented.

papers.title: Sequential Meridian Based Acupuncture Combined With Standard Rehabilitation After Surgery for Severe Cubital Tunnel Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.journal: Annals of plastic surgery
papers.authors: Ding L, Zhang Q, Si Y, Zhou H, Chen Z, Qu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
To evaluate the efficacy of sequential meridian-based acupuncture combined with standard rehabilitation in patients after surgery for severe cubital tunnel syndrome (CuTS).
In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 40 patients with severe CuTS who underwent ulnar nerve decompression with subfascial anterior transposition combined with supercharged end-to-side nerve transfers (the pronator quadratus branch and the abductor digiti minimi branch to the deep branch of the ulnar nerve) were randomly assigned to a sequential acupuncture group and a standard rehabilitation group (n=20). The standard rehabilitation group received neurotrophic medication and progressive rehabilitation training; the sequential acupuncture group additionally received staged meridian-based acupuncture (the Small Intestine Meridian and the Triple Energizer Meridian were primarily selected during postoperative months 0 to 3, supplemented by the Large Intestine Meridian thereafter, combining filiform-needle acupuncture and electroacupuncture). Motor nerve conduction velocity (MCV), sensory nerve conduction velocity (SCV), lateral pinch strength ratio, ring-finger grip strength ratio, 2-point discrimination (2PD), DASH score, EQ-5D-5L score, and VAS score were assessed preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively.
Thirty-seven patients completed follow-up (18 in the sequential acupuncture group and 19 in the standard rehabilitation group; overall dropout rate 7.5%), with no acupuncture-related adverse events. Baseline characteristics were balanced between the 2 groups (P>0.05). Beginning at 3 months postoperatively, improvements in MCV, lateral pinch strength ratio, ring-finger grip strength ratio, DASH score, and EQ-5D-5L score were greater in the sequential acupuncture group than in the standard rehabilitation group (P<0.05), with between-group differences widening at 6 months (P<0.01). Group×time interactions were significant for these 6 indicators (P<0.001), and between-group differences in improvement magnitude reached large effect sizes (MCV: MD=5.80 m/s, 95% CI: 4.70-6.90; SCV: MD=4.65 m/s, 95% CI: 3.30-6.01; lateral pinch strength ratio: d=2.165; ring-finger grip strength ratio: d=2.321). No significant between-group differences were observed in ring-finger or little-finger 2PD or in VAS score at any time point (P>0.05).
Sequential meridian-based acupuncture combined with standard rehabilitation accelerates postoperative electrophysiological and intrinsic hand muscle recovery and improves upper-limb function and quality of life in patients with severe CuTS. The therapeutic advantage emerges during postoperative months 3 to 6, the critical window of nerve regeneration, with a favorable safety profile.

papers.title: Neuropeptides in Immunometabolism and Neuroinflammation: Insights from Traditional Chinese Medicine.
papers.journal: Neuroendocrinology
papers.authors: Wu CH, Cheng CF, Nguyen TKN, Su LY, Lee MC, Chuang WC
papers.abstract: Neuropeptides are small bioactive peptides secreted by neurons and immune cells that serve as critical messengers in both central and peripheral systems. Recent studies have identified key neuropeptides-such as Substance P (SP), Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide (VIP), Neuropeptide Y (NPY), and Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide (CGRP)-as pivotal regulators of immunometabolism and neuroinflammation. These peptides influence macrophage polarization, T cell differentiation, cytokine production, and neuroimmune crosstalk, linking chronic inflammation to conditions such as obesity, diabetes, autoimmunity, and neurodegeneration. This review synthesizes emerging evidence on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) interventions-including herbal formulas, single herbs, bioactive compounds, and acupuncture-that modulate neuropeptide signaling via NF-κB, MAPK, and Nrf2 pathways. These mechanisms contribute to analgesia, emotional stabilization, metabolic regulation, and neuroprotection. The article further presents a modular framework connecting representative Chinese medicinal substances to specific neuropeptides and physiological functions, offering a translational foundation for neuropeptide-targeted therapies and integrative precision health strategies.

papers.title: Baihe Zhimu Decoction ameliorates anxious depression via PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway-mediated neuroprotection and inhibition of hippocampal neuronal apoptosis.
papers.journal: Animal models and experimental medicine
papers.authors: Han Y, He K, Yang H, Dai J, Chen R, Liu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Anxious depression involves severe emotional dysregulation with a high risk of relapse and suicide. Although the classical Traditional Chinese Medicine formula Baihe Zhimu Decoction (BZD) is widely used for affective disorders, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.
In this study, the chemical constituents of BZD were first identified using UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, followed by a maximum-dose safety evaluation. The therapeutic effects of BZD were then investigated in an anxious-depression mouse model induced by chronic restraint stress (CRS) combined with corticosterone (CORT) administration. Behavioral assessments, including the open field test (OFT), elevated plus maze (EPM), sucrose preference test (SPT), and forced swim test (FST), were performed, together with histopathological examination of hippocampal tissues. Network pharmacology was employed to analyze the relationships between active compounds and potential targets and to predict related signaling pathways. Subsequently, western blot analysis, immunofluorescence staining, Hoechst staining, and flow cytometry, combined with pathway-specific inhibitors, were used to examine the involvement of the signaling pathway in hippocampal tissues and primary hippocampal neurons.
Forty-one constituents were identified in BZD. In vivo results showed that BZD significantly alleviated hippocampal pathological injury and improved anxiety- and depression-like behaviors in stressed mice. Network pharmacology analysis identified 19 active compounds and 622 potential targets, highlighting the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. Mechanistically, BZD activated this pathway and protected against neuronal injury, while these effects were attenuated by the PI3K inhibitor LY294002.
BZD exerts potent neuroprotective and therapeutic effects against anxious depression, primarily driven by activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and preserving hippocampal neuronal integrity.

papers.title: Elucidating the multi-target therapeutic mechanism of Kangtai decoction in lung cancer through integrated network pharmacology and molecular docking.
papers.journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
papers.authors: Niu J, Yang Y, Hui Y, Feng C
papers.abstract:
Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, with a high incidence and limited effective treatments, the main focus being on symptom management and tumor control. Kangtai decoction (KTD), a traditional Chinese medicine, has shown promising results in alleviating lung cancer symptoms and improving quality of life in China, though its precise mechanism of action remains unclear.
This study employed a network pharmacology-based approach, complemented by molecular docking, to identify the bioactive components, key targets, and potential pharmacological mechanisms of KTD against lung cancer.
Bioactive components and drug targets of KTD, along with targets related to lung cancer, were collected from public databases. Bioinformatics analyses, including protein-protein interaction (PPI), gene ontology (GO), and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analyses, were conducted to identify core targets, bioactive components, and signaling pathways. Molecular docking was then performed to predict the binding between active compounds and core targets.
A total of 145 effective components of KTD for treating lung cancer were screened, along with 113 common targets between KTD and lung cancer. Bioinformatics analysis and molecular docking indicated that in the treatment of lung cancer with KTD, neocryptotanshinone II was the most significant bioactive compound, IL1B was the most pivotal target, and the IL-17 signaling pathway was the most critical pathway.
KTD is effective in the treatment of lung cancer, possibly because of the binding of its active components to key therapeutic targets involved in lung cancer.
