papers.title: Acupuncture and Moxibustion for Neck Pain: A Clinical Practice Guideline.
papers.journal: Journal of evidence-based medicine
papers.authors: Wang Y, Yin Z, Sun X, Liang F, Zhao J, Zhu L et al.
papers.abstract:
Neck pain (NP) is a leading cause of disability worldwide. Pharmacological treatments often provide limited benefits and may be associated with adverse effects, highlighting the need for effective non-pharmacological options.
To develop evidence-based recommendations on the effectiveness, safety, and clinical implementation of acupuncture and/or moxibustion for adults with NP.
This guideline was developed in accordance with the Reporting Items for practice Guidelines in HealThcare (RIGHT) statement for acupuncture and the BMJ Rapid Recommendations process. Recommendations were informed by a systematic review of 88 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 10,172 participants. Evidence certainty was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE), and recommendations were formulated through an evidence-to-decision framework and multidisciplinary consensus.
The guideline proposed five recommendations: (1) acupuncture and/or moxibustion is suggested rather than no such treatment (weak recommendation, moderate-certainty); (2) acupuncture and/or moxibustion may be considered for patients with moderate-to-severe pain or prolonged symptoms (weak recommendation, low-certainty); (3) adding acupuncture and/or moxibustion to usual care is suggested rather than usual care alone (weak recommendation, low-certainty); (4) an initial 3-4-week course, using 5-10 acupoints/session and 3-5 sessions/week, may serve as a reference regimen (weak recommendation, low-certainty); and (5) electroacupuncture may be preferentially considered for pain relief and functional improvement, whereas manual acupuncture, warm needling, and moxibustion may be alternatives (weak recommendation, low-certainty). Adverse events were generally mild and self-limiting.
Acupuncture and/or moxibustion may be reasonable and safe non-pharmacological options for adults with NP. Clinical use should be guided by shared decision-making that considers symptom severity, disease duration, treatment goals, patient preferences, accessibility, and practitioner expertise.

papers.title: Gardenia jasminoides Ellis 70% ethanolic fraction alleviates hyperuricemia by upregulating PPARγ and modulating its downstream urate transporters and anti-inflammatory pathways.
papers.journal: Journal of ethnopharmacology
papers.authors: Li R, Chen G, Li Y, Liu H, Huang L, Yang C et al.
papers.abstract:
Gardenia jasminoides Ellis (GJE) is a traditional Chinese medicine widely used for metabolic disorders. However, its efficacy against hyperuricemia, the responsible active fraction, and the underlying mechanisms of its effect remains to be clarified.
To investigate the material basis and urate-lowering activity of the 70% ethanolic fraction of GJE (GJE70), and to elucidate its molecular mechanism.
UPLC-Q-TOF-MS characterized the chemical composition of GJE70. Hyperuricemia was induced in rats by potassium oxonate and yeast extract. Serum and urinary uric acid, uric acid clearance, renal function, and histopathology were assessed for anti-hyperuricemia efficacy and urate excretion. Hepatic function and histology were examined for safety. To explore mechanisms, kidney transcriptomics and metabolomics were performed; molecular docking predicted compound-target binding, which was validated by IF, WB, qRT-PCR and rescue experiments in HK-2 cells.
UPLC-Q-TOF-MS identified 18 major compounds in GJE70, with crocins predominant. In hyperuricemia rats, GJE70 significantly reduced serum uric acid and increased urinary uric acid excretion and clearance, indicating enhanced renal urate elimination. Renal function and histopathology showed alleviated renal injury without obvious hepatotoxicity, with normal liver enzymes and histology. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that GJE70 mainly modulated PPAR signaling pathways. Molecular docking and MD Analysis demonstrated strong binding affinities of compounds to PPARγ. Subsequent IF, WB, and qRT-PCR confirmed that GJE70 upregulated PPARγ expression and its downstream urate transporters (ABCG2, OAT1, and OAT3), and suppressed NF-κB signaling levels. In HK-2 cells, GJE70 reduced supernatant uric acid, upregulated ABCG2/OAT1/OAT3, and inhibited NF-κB activation; GW9662 attenuated these effects, confirming PPARγ dependence.
GJE70 exerts potent urate-lowering and renoprotective effects via PPARγ-mediated regulation of urate transporters and anti-inflammatory pathways, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for hyperuricemia.

papers.title: Oxysophocarpine attenuates acute liver injury by targeting FBP1 to suppress ferroptosis and enhance cellular resilience via the PPARα-GPX4 axis.
papers.journal: Free radical biology & medicine
papers.authors: Shi J, Liu Y, Wang R, Li X, Jiang Y, Yu J et al.
papers.abstract: Acute liver injury (ALI) is a life-threatening clinical condition with limited therapeutic options. Through network pharmacology screening, we identified oxysophocarpine (OSC), a natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine, as a potent reactive oxygen species-scavenging agent. In LPS/D-GalN-induced ALI models, OSC administration dose-dependently improved survival, attenuated histopathological damage, reduced serum transaminase levels and inflammatory cytokines, and enhanced antioxidant capacity. Notably, we report for the first time that OSC directly bound to fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase (FBP1) and modulated its interaction with peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα), leading to upregulated glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) expression and subsequent inhibition of ferroptosis, apoptosis, and endoplasmic reticulum stress. Collectively, this study reveals a multidimensional protective mechanism of OSC against ALI centered on FBP1 targeting, integrating anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-cell death activities, thereby providing a rationale for developing OSC as a promising natural product-based therapy for ALI.

papers.title: Ejiao (Asini Corii Colla) promotes thin endometrium repair via upregulation of the SDF-1/CXCR4 signalling axis in a mouse model.
papers.journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
papers.authors: Tan M, Wei H, Wei D, Lai T, Xiao J
papers.abstract:
Thin endometrium (TE) severely impairs embryo implantation and pregnancy outcomes in reproductive medicine, while first-line oestrogen-based therapy has marked limitations including receptor insensitivity and systemic side effects. Ejiao (Asini Corii Colla), a classic Traditional Chinese Medicine tonic, is widely used for gynecological disorders, yet its mechanism in endometrial regeneration remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effect of Ejiao on TE and its regulation of the SDF-1/CXCR4 signalling axis.
A TE mouse model was established via intrauterine infusion of 95% ethanol in female C57BL/6J mice. Mice were randomly divided into 4 groups (n = 6 per group): sham operation control group, TE model group, oestradiol positive control group (0.04 mg/kg/d), and Ejiao intervention group (0.2 g/kg/d), with 4 weeks of daily gavage intervention. Oestrous cycle stability was verified by vaginal smears, endometrial morphology was evaluated by HE staining, and SDF-1/CXCR4 mRNA expression in uterine tissues was detected by qPCR.
All mice maintained stable oestrous cycling throughout the experiment. Ejiao treatment markedly restored endometrial thickness and glandular density in TE mice, with a superior reparative effect to oestradiol, and significantly upregulated the mRNA expression of SDF-1 and CXCR4 in uterine tissue (P < 0.05 vs. model and oestradiol groups).
Ejiao effectively promotes endometrial regeneration in TE mice via upregulating the SDF-1/CXCR4 signalling axis, providing preclinical mechanistic evidence for its clinical application in TE treatment.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture synergizes with anti-ferroptosis bioelectrical niche remodeling to promote spinal cord regeneration.
papers.journal: Materials today. Bio
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Mo Y, Yan B, Wang X, Wu P, Wu Y et al.
papers.abstract: Severe spinal cord injury (SCI) frequently causes persistent neurological deficits, and its repair is constrained by multiple pathological factors including deterioration of the microenvironment following secondary injury, massive neuronal loss, interruption of electrical signal conduction, and insufficient endogenous regenerative capacity. Although electroacupuncture (EA) participates in the rehabilitation of SCI by regulating inflammatory responses and promoting the secretion of neurotrophic factors, standalone EA therapy can hardly fully reverse oxidative stress, ferroptosis and neural circuit destruction following severe SCI. Accordingly, this study constructs a conductive anti-ferroptosis hydrogel system (HBP@BMSCs), which utilizes dopamine-grafted hyaluronic acid (HADA) as the bionic matrix, baicalin-polypyrrole (BA-PPy) as the functional component, and is loaded with bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). This hydrogel system is combined with EA for the repair of severe SCI. The results demonstrate that the HBP hydrogel exhibits favorable cytocompatibility, which can support the survival of BMSCs and maintain their typical mesenchymal stem cell phenotype. In vitro experiments demonstrate that HBP hydrogel effectively alleviates TBHP-induced oxidative stress injury and Erastin-induced ferroptosis-related injury, and exerts a protective effect on BMSCs and PC12 cells. In vivo experiments further confirmed that the combination therapy of HBP@BMSCs with EA significantly downregulated the expression levels of 4HNE, COX2, NOX2, FTH, FTL and TFR after SCI, and restored the expression levels of XCT, GPX4, SOD1 and FPN, thereby alleviating ROS accumulation, lipid peroxidation, iron overload and ferroptosis. With the alleviation of oxidative stress and ferroptosis-related secondary damage, the combination therapy further downregulates the expression of Bax and C-caspase3, upregulates Bcl-2 levels, and significantly inhibits neuronal apoptosis. In addition, the BA-PPy conductive network can synergize with EA to enhance electrical stimulation conduction, upregulate NGF/NGFR and BDNF neurotrophic signaling pathways, and promote the neural lineage differentiation of BMSCs, axon regeneration, corticospinal tract (CST) remodeling, and the recovery of motor function. In conclusion, HBP@BMSCs combined with EA exerts multiple synergistic effects including microenvironment remodeling, anti-ferroptosis protection, stem cell delivery and electroactive neural regeneration, providing a comprehensive therapeutic strategy with translational potential for severe SCI repair.

papers.title: Comprehensive Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies Potential Biomarkers and Underlying Mechanisms of Acupuncture in Treating Peripheral Facial Paralysis.
papers.journal: Journal of molecular neuroscience : MN
papers.authors: Li X, Li Y, Zou X, Liu J, Yin R, Wei Q et al.
papers.abstract: Peripheral facial palsy (PFP) is a common neurological disorder. Acupuncture is an effective therapeutic intervention, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely elucidated. To evaluate the clinical efficacy of acupuncture for PFP and to identify differentially expressed RNAs and associated pathways via whole transcriptome analysis, thereby revealing potential molecular mechanisms. Clinical efficacy was assessed using the House-Brackmann (HB) scale, Facial Disability Index (FDI), and comprehensive traditional Chinese medicine efficacy criteria. Peripheral blood samples were collected from patients before and after acupuncture treatment. Differentially expressed circRNAs, lncRNAs, miRNAs, and mRNAs were screened through whole transcriptome sequencing. Bioinformatics analyses were employed to construct a competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network and perform Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analyses. Acupuncture significantly improved clinical scores post-treatment. A total of 1625 differentially expressed mRNAs (1153 up-, 472 down-regulated), 715 lncRNAs (321 up-, 394 down-regulated), 85 circRNAs (56 up-, 29 down-regulated), and 253 miRNAs (141 up-, 112 down-regulated) were identified. The ceRNA network revealed that non-coding RNAs competitively bind key miRNA molecules, forming two distinct and independent regulatory axes that precisely modulate downstream target genes. KEGG enrichment analysis of core molecular targets indicated significant involvement in the Olfactory transduction and JAK-STAT signaling pathways. Acupuncture may exert its therapeutic effect on PFP by modulating the ceRNA network, alongside the Olfactory transduction and JAK-STAT signaling pathways, synergistically promoting nerve regeneration and suppressing neuroinflammation.

papers.title: Terpenes and terpenoids modulating TRPV channels in diabetes: role in fibrosis and inflammatory signaling.
papers.journal: Molecular biology reports
papers.authors: Awate SA, Kaur G
papers.abstract: Transient receptor potential vanilloid (TRPV) channels are non-selective cation channels that mediate thermosensation, nociception, osmotic balance, and metabolic regulation. In diabetes, altered TRPV channel expression and decreased calcium influx key pathways modulates, include NF-κB, AMPK, and TGF-β, promoting extracellular matrix accumulation and fibrotic remodelling. The limited availability of pathway specific interventions highlights TRPV channels as potential therapeutic target in diabetes. Recently, natural phytoconstituents have shown to exhibit TRPV channel modulating properties. Studies also highlights the potential of terpenes and terpenoids to inhibit NF-κB mediated inflammation, and activate AMPK-promoted metabolic homeostasis, mitigating diabetes-associated tissue damage. Preclinical studies have explored major terpenoids such as d-limonene, p-cymene and carvacrol in diabetic models. These compounds have been reported to improve glucose tolerance and alter the blood glucose levels via different molecular mechanisms. Clinically, there are limited evidences reporting terpenoids in the metabolic syndrome and TRPV modulation. Example, Astaxanthin, a tetraterpenoid has multiple human trials in type 2 diabetes, reducing diabetic biomarkers like SIRT1, HbA1c, and fasting glucose. This review summarizes current evidence on terpenes and terpenoids in diabetes with their reported and proposed interactions with TRPV1, TRPV4 with particular emphasis on their potential links to oxidative stress, NF-κB-mediated inflammation, TGF-β-associated fibrosis, and metabolic signaling. By distinguishing experimentally supported TRPV modulation with mechanistic associations and which require further validation, this review provides an integrated framework for understanding potential contribution of terpenoid-TRPV interactions to diabetes progression and its inflammatory and fibrotic complications, while highlighting key gaps for future experimental and translational investigation.

papers.title: Ginseng alleviates fatigue by inhibiting autophagy via activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway.
papers.journal: Molecular biology reports
papers.authors: Liu H, Xiong R, Zhang S, Zhang P, Wang L, Wang Q et al.
papers.abstract:
Panax ginseng C. A. Mey. (PG) is a commonly used traditional Chinese medicine to relieve fatigue-related symptoms. However, the underlying mechanisms by which PG alleviates fatigue are still not fully understood. This study aims to elucidate the anti-fatigue mechanism of PG in a hyperammonemia induced fatigue mouse model.
The therapeutic effects of PG on hyperammonemia-induced fatigue mice were evaluated using behavioral assessments, including rotarod, open field, grip strength, and tail suspension tests, along with serum biochemical analysis and hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining. To investigate the molecular mechanisms, an integrated approach combining transcriptomics, proteomics, network pharmacology, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, and Western blot was employed.
PG significantly enhanced the exercise tolerance of hyperammonemia-induced fatigue mice, ameliorated skeletal muscle fiber atrophy, and restored the serum ammonia, creatine kinase, blood urea nitrogen, lactate dehydrogenase, and blood glucose levels. Comprehensive analysis of transcriptomics, proteomics and network pharmacology indicated that the mechanism of anti-fatigue of PG may be mediated by regulating autophagy via the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. In addition, immunohistochemistry, Western blot, and immunofluorescence analysis confirmed that PG protected against fatigue by activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway to restore dysregulated autophagy in skeletal muscle under hyperammonemia conditions.
PG may alleviate fatigue by inhibiting excessive autophagy via the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and restoring the protein balance within skeletal muscle.

papers.title: Prevalence and independent influencing factors of moderate-to-severe cancer-related fatigue (CRF) and its association with Buzhong-Yiqi (BZYQ) use among patients with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma (LACSCC): a retrospective observational study using propensity-score weighting (PSW) logistic regression model.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
papers.authors: Li C, Luo Z, Tian L, Deng W, Pang Q, Bentley GT et al.
papers.abstract:
Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is a debilitating syndrome in cervical cancer patients, resistant to conventional bedrest. This study analyzed CRF drivers and observed the real-world correlation of the Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulation, Buzhong Yiqi, in the incidence of the moderate-to-severe CRF patients with stage IIB-IVA cervical carcinoma.
This was a retrospective observational study conducted at Chengdu Xinjin District People's Hospital and Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital. According to inclusion and exclusion criteria, we enrolled patients diagnosed with stage IIB-IVA cervical squamous carcinoma (FIGO 2018 criteria). We identified factors influencing CRF severity using Electronic Medical Records and patient questionnaires. The prevalence of CRF was estimated among patients diagnosed with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma (LACSCC). According to the univariate and multivariate analysis, we want to find the independent influencing factors of moderate-to-severe CRF. Independent sample t-tests and Chi-squared tests were performed to assess differences in symptom scores between BZYQ (Buzhong-Yiqi)-treated and non BZYQ-treated groups. A propensity score-weighted(PSW) logistic regression model was employed to evaluate the association between the real-world BZYQ treatment and the risk of moderate-to-severe CRF.
We enrolled 144 patients diagnosed with stage IIB-IVA cervical squamous carcinoma (FIGO 2018 criteria) who underwent chemoradiation, chemotherapy alone, radiation therapy alone, targeting therapy or no anticancer treatment. Among them, 50% had moderate-to-severe CRF. Independent factors significantly influencing the incidence of moderate-to-severe CRF included disease stage (P = 0.001), Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status (ECOG-PS) (P = 0.003), cancer pain (P < 0.001), anemia (P < 0.001), poor appetite (P < 0.001), proactive clinician attention (P = 0.042) and BZYQ treatment (P = 0.001). After propensity-score weighting, the BZYQ-treatment group exhibited a 68.3% reduction in the odds of moderate to severe CRF (OR = 0.317; P < 0.001).
CRF is a complex, multifactorial syndrome driven by tumor burden, synergistic symptoms, and quality of supportive care. Among patients with LACSCC, CRF is common. In clinical practice, CRF should be included in routine screening to achieve early identification and early intervention. Throughout the course of diagnosis and treatment, long-term dynamic assessment and timely interventions should be implemented for modifiable risk factors such as cancer-related pain, anemia and poor appetite, so as to reduce the risk and severity of CRF. Meanwhile, clinicians should actively attend to patients' complaints of fatigue and strengthen awareness for the identification and standardized management of this symptom. This real-world observational study suggests that BZYQ treatment is correlated with the decreased incidence of moderate-to-severe CRF, providing preliminary clues for further exploring its application value in CRF management.

papers.title: Deciphering the mechanisms of resveratrol in knee osteoarthritis treatment: insights from bioinformatics and experimental validation.
papers.journal: Naunyn-Schmiedeberg's archives of pharmacology
papers.authors: Huang C, Ye X, Liu X, Liu F, Li Y, Chen X et al.
papers.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is the most prevalent chronic joint disorder in orthopedics, with its underlying pathogenic genes and effective treatment methods remaining unclear. Resveratrol (RES), a potent bioactive natural polyphenol, has been shown to effectively alleviate KOA; however, its complex regulatory mechanisms require further investigation. This research seeks to clarify the molecular mechanisms by which RES contributes to the treatment of KOA, utilizing a blend of bioinformatics approaches and experimental validation. First, gene expression profiles related to KOA were obtained from the GEO database. Subsequently, differential gene analysis was conducted on the samples, and modular genes linked to KOA were extracted through the application of a weighted gene co-expression network. The LASSO algorithm was utilized to identify crucial pathogenic genes in KOA, which were later confirmed using clinical samples. Targets for RES were sourced from traditional Chinese medicine databases, and the therapeutic targets for KOA treatment were determined by finding the intersection of these sources. An enrichment analysis was carried out based on the therapeutic targets identified. Molecular docking studies were conducted to further assess the binding affinity of key therapeutic genes with RES. Lastly, animal experiments were implemented to substantiate the molecular mechanisms by which RES acts in the treatment of KOA. We identified 460 module genes and 10 key predictive genes through LASSO analysis. The findings from the enrichment analysis concerning potential therapeutic targets for RES in the treatment of KOA reveal that the significant genes implicated include VEGFA, IL6, MAPK3, IL1B, CASP3, and AKT1. Subsequent validation with clinical samples revealed that IL6, MAPK3, IL1B, CASP3, and AKT1 were significantly elevated during the progression of KOA, while VEGFA was markedly reduced in the context of KOA. The outcomes of the GO and KEGG analyses suggest that the primary biological processes implicated encompass apoptosis, the FoxO signaling pathway, the IL-17 signaling pathway, cellular senescence, and the NF-κB signaling pathway. The findings from the immune infiltration analysis indicate that resting CD4 memory T cells, memory B cells, resting mast cells, eosinophils, and activated mast cells may have important functions in the immune mechanisms related to KOA. The results of animal experiments demonstrate that RES effectively inhibits the expression of inflammatory factors such as IL-6, MAPK3, IL-1β, CASP3, and AKT1 during the progression of KOA, promotes the expression of VEGFA, and concurrently suppresses the FoxO signaling pathway and the IL-17 signaling pathway, thereby reducing cartilage damage induced by MIA and delaying the progression of KOA. In summary, RES can regulate the expression of genes including VEGFA, IL-6, MAPK3, IL-1β, CASP3, and AKT1, inhibit the FoxO signaling pathway and the IL-17 signaling pathway, alleviate cartilage damage induced by MIA, and delay the progression of KOA.

papers.title: Sequential stage-specific administration of Bushen-Tiaojing decoctions II and III ameliorates mitochondrial dysfunction in ovarian granulosa cells of COH mice by regulating GRP75-mediated MAM homeostasis.
papers.journal: Journal of ethnopharmacology
papers.authors: Ding X, Wen X, Xiong W, Liu H, Tang S, Li D et al.
papers.abstract:
Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) offers a distinct therapeutic approach to infertility. Bushen-Tiaojing Decoctions II (BSTJ-II-D) and III (BSTJ-III-D; collectively, BSTJD) are clinical formulas developed by Professor Huilan Du according to the TCM theory of stage-specific treatment and are widely used in the clinical management of infertility. Previous studies have shown that sequential, stage-specific administration of these formulas can improve mitochondrial energy metabolism and increase pregnancy rates among infertile women undergoing in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF-ET). However, whether this sequential treatment improves mitochondrial function in ovarian granulosa cells (GCs) by preserving mitochondria-associated endoplasmic reticulum membrane (MAM) homeostasis remains unclear.
Glucose-regulated protein 75 (GRP75) is a key tethering protein that maintains MAM homeostasis. This study aimed to determine whether sequential, stage-specific administration of BSTJ-II-D and BSTJ-III-D ameliorates mitochondrial dysfunction in ovarian GCs by regulating GRP75-mediated MAM homeostasis.
A controlled ovarian hyperstimulation (COH) mouse model was established, after which animals received BSTJ-II-D and BSTJ-III-D sequentially via oral gavage. A group treated with GRP75-IN-1, a novel small-molecule compound that targets and binds GRP75, was included as a control. MAM morphology, mitochondrial bioenergetic activity, and mitochondrial biogenesis were systematically evaluated. For the in vitro experiments, human KGN ovarian granulosa-like tumor cells were transduced with a GRP75-overexpressing lentiviral construct to clarify how elevated GRP75 expression affects MAM architecture and function and subsequently influences mitochondrial homeostasis. Protein levels of GRP75, voltage-dependent anion channel 1 (VDAC1), mitochondrial calcium uniporter (MCU), sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ coactivator 1-α (PGC-1α), and nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) were assessed in GCs. Cellular adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, mitochondrial Ca2+ loading, and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) were determined using fluorescence-based assays. In addition, mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opening was evaluated quantitatively by flow cytometric analysis.
Sequential BSTJD treatment attenuated COH-induced aberrant GRP75 overexpression, restored MAM ultrastructural integrity, reduced mitochondrial oxidative stress (OS) and Ca2+ overload, and enhanced mitochondrial energy metabolism and biogenesis. Mechanistically, BSTJD increased the expression of SIRT1, PGC-1α, and Nrf2 while inhibiting activation of the PERK/ATF4 pathway, thereby alleviating endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and enhancing mitochondrial energy metabolism and biogenesis. GRP75-IN-1 reproduced the protective effects of BSTJD. Conversely, GRP75 overexpression in KGN cells disrupted MAMs and impaired mitochondrial function, further supporting GRP75 as a key mediator of the protective effects of BSTJD.
Sequential BSTJD treatment preserves MAM homeostasis by suppressing aberrant GRP75 overexpression, thereby mitigating OS and mitochondrial Ca2+ overload. It also activates the SIRT1-PGC-1α-Nrf2 pathway to restore mitochondrial energy metabolism and biogenesis, ultimately ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction in GCs. These findings provide new molecular evidence supporting the Bushen Tiaojing therapeutic approach for infertility.

papers.title: Glycocalyx-binding and cell-penetrating peptide-modified nanomicelles for enhanced ocular delivery of quercetin and retinal protection in a dAMD model.
papers.journal: International journal of pharmaceutics
papers.authors: Li S, Yang Q, Zhu Y, Li T, Scherman D, Li W et al.
papers.abstract: Dry age-related macular degeneration (dAMD) is a highly prevalent degenerative retinal disease. Quercetin, a bioactive ingredient in traditional Chinese medicine, can mitigate the oxidative stress that helps drive dAMD; however, its low water solubility and poor corneal permeability limit its efficacy. We developed dual-functional polymeric micelles (PMs) co-conjugated with a glycocalyx-binding peptide (GBP) and a cell-penetrating peptide (TAT) for the enhanced topical ocular delivery of quercetin (QUE), named GT-PMs/QUE. The GT-PMs/QUE exhibited a particle size of 46.25 ± 3.05 nm and a zeta potential of -5.64 ± 0.92 mV. GT-PMs exhibited significantly higher cellular uptake efficiency than the unmodified group (PMs) and single-peptide modified groups (GBP-PMs and TAT-PMs). In the sodium iodate-induced oxidative damage model of adult retinal pigment epithelial cell line-19 (ARPE-19) cells, the GT-PMs/QUE treatment group showed significantly reduced ROS and MDA levels along with markedly increased SOD, CAT, and GSH activities that approached normal control levels compared to the model group. In a mouse model of dAMD, GT-PMs/QUE greatly improved the bioavailability of quercetin delivered via eye drop administration and attenuated sodium iodate-induced retinal damage. This study provides a theoretical and experimental basis for enhanced ocular delivery of quercetin and protection against dAMD-related retinal damage.

papers.title: Acupuncture Attenuates Myopia Progression by Suppressing Scleral Inflammation and Enhancing Neurotrophic Signaling.
papers.journal: Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE
papers.authors: Zhang J, Zhou Y, Wang Y, Xu W, Shangguan Y, Li B et al.
papers.abstract: Myopia is a common ocular disorder characterized by excessive axial elongation, and effective strategies for limiting its progression remain limited. This study investigated whether acupuncture attenuates myopia progression in a guinea pig model of form-deprivation myopia and examined the involvement of scleral inflammation and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-mediated neurotrophic signaling. Guinea pigs were randomly assigned to control, myopia, acupuncture-only, and myopia plus acupuncture groups for phenotypic evaluation. Additional sham acupuncture and myopia-plus-acupuncture groups, combined with subconjunctival cyclotraxin B (CTX-B) administration, were included to evaluate acupuncture specificity and the involvement of BDNF/tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB) signaling. Following intervention, refractive error and axial length were measured in the primary treatment groups. Scleral remodeling markers, including collagen type I alpha 1 (COL1A1) and α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA); inflammatory mediators, including interleukin-1β (IL-1β), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB); and neurotrophic factors, including BDNF, TrkB, nerve growth factor, and neurotrophin-4, were evaluated using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, quantitative reverse transcription PCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. Acupuncture was associated with reduced myopic refractive shifts and axial elongation. At the final observation time point, axial elongation was lower in the myopia plus acupuncture group than in the myopia group (ΔAL, 0.77 ± 0.19 mm vs. 1.42 ± 0.20 mm; Cohen's d = 1.51). Acupuncture also reduced scleral IL-1β, IL-6, and NF-κB expression and increased BDNF, TrkB, nerve growth factor, and neurotrophin-4 expression. Sham acupuncture showed limited effects on these molecular changes, whereas CTX-B attenuated acupuncture-associated alterations in BDNF/TrkB signaling, extracellular matrix remodeling, and inflammatory markers. These findings suggest that acupuncture attenuates myopia progression through coordinated regulation of scleral inflammation and neurotrophic support involving BDNF/TrkB signaling.

papers.title: Evaluating Macrophage Polarization and Inflammation in Bitongqing-Treated Collagen-Induced Arthritis Rats.
papers.journal: Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE
papers.authors: Pan J, Zhu W, Liu C, Wu Y, Zhao J, Wang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent synovial inflammation and immune dysregulation. Traditional Chinese medicine formulas such as Bitongqing Decoction (BTQ) are used clinically, but reproducible workflows are needed to characterize their absorbed constituents and associated immunological effects. This article presents an integrated protocol comprising herbal preparation, collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) induction, 21-day oral treatment, serum ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole-Orbitrap mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS), arthritis scoring, micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), hematoxylin and eosin staining, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and western blotting. The workflow evaluates macroscopic disease manifestations, joint pathology, inflammatory mediators, macrophage-associated M1-like and M2-like markers, splenic T helper 1 (Th1)- and regulatory T cell (Treg)-associated markers, and NF-κB/MAPK signaling proteins. Representative data showed that BTQ treatment was associated with improved arthritis-related outcomes, lower levels of inflammatory mediators, reduced CD80, iNOS, MHCII, and STAT1 signaling, increased CD163 and ARG-1 signaling, altered CXCR3 and FOXP3 signaling, and reduced phosphorylation of P65, ERK, and JNK. Because marker intensities, rather than cell-number ratios, were measured, these findings are described as changes in marker profiles rather than as direct measurements of M1/M2 or Th1/Treg balance. This protocol provides a multimodal framework for pharmacological studies of complex herbal formulas by linking the characterization of circulating constituents with structural, histological, and immunological readouts while preserving physiological interactions among synovial macrophages, lymphocytes, fibroblast-like synoviocytes, and other joint-resident cells.

summary.clinical_takeaway: 복합 한약 처방의 전임상 약리평가에서 순환 성분 분석과 구조·조직·면역 지표를 함께 보는 다중모달 접근이 유용할 수 있다.
summary.limitations: 마커 강도 변화만 측정하여 M1/M2 또는 Th1/Treg 비율의 직접 측정으로 해석할 수 없다는 점에 주의가 필요하다.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine as Adjunctive Care in Cancer and Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Narrative Review of Shared Frameworks and Evidence Gaps.
papers.journal: Journal of visualized experiments : JoVE
papers.authors: Li B, Xu X
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has increasingly been investigated as an adjunctive approach to conventional treatment in chronic and complex diseases, including cancer and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Although cancer and RA differ substantially in pathogenesis and therapeutic goals, both are associated with persistent symptom burden, treatment-related adverse effects, impaired physical function, psychological distress, and long-term supportive-care needs. This narrative review evaluates TCM within this shared adjunctive-care framework while maintaining disease-specific interpretation of the available evidence. In cancer, TCM-related interventions have been investigated for supportive symptom management, pain relief, treatment tolerance, quality-of-life improvement, and potential modulation of biological processes, including apoptosis, angiogenesis, immune regulation, invasion, metastasis, and multidrug resistance. In RA, Chinese herbal medicines, acupuncture, and related approaches have been evaluated for their potential effects on pain, inflammation, physical function, bone remodeling, and early disease-related processes. TCM-related mind-body practices, such as qigong and tai chi, may also provide psychological support, whereas mindfulness-based interventions are considered supportive-care strategies rather than TCM interventions. Current evidence ranges from mechanistic and preclinical studies to observational studies, single-arm clinical studies, randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses, with substantial variation in methodological quality. Overall, TCM should be considered a potential complement to, rather than a replacement for, established oncological or rheumatological treatment. Further well-designed clinical studies, standardized interventions, rigorous quality control, safety monitoring, and clinically meaningful outcome assessment are required to define its appropriate role in multidisciplinary care.
